title: Add taxonomy-driven profile assembler and auto release brief
author: Priya Ramesh
release_notes: Adds a taxonomy-driven normalizer to map incoming model metadata into canonical profile fields; introduces an autosummary writer that drafts compact release briefs for new model versions to reduce manual changelog work. No runtime behavior changes; backward-compatible with existing profile schema.
description: Context and motivation: onboarding runs into inconsistent vendor metadata (variant labels, capability tags, dataset attributions). This causes noisy profiles and manual cleanup during release note composition. This PR implements a taxonomy-driven profile assembler that maps diverse intake attributes into the canonical model profile schema, plus an auto release brief generator that produces a concise changelog bullet and a human-editable template. Goals: (1) Reduce manual curation time for new model intake; (2) Improve stability of changelog generation and reduce release-author friction; (3) Make downstream tooling (profiling, compatibility heuristics) rely on a consistent ontology. What changed: - New module registry/taxonomy/assembler.py: core mapper that takes raw intake JSON and a taxonomy config and produces normalized profile fields (capabilities, hardware_affinity, license_section, sample_dataset_refs). Mapping rules are composable and support fallback heuristics and confidence scoring. - New module registry/autobreif/writer.py: templated brief generator that consumes normalized profile and sampled telemetry to emit a short release blurb (title, one-line summary, perf highlights, stability signal). - New config: registry/taxonomy/standard_taxonomy.yaml with initial canonical tags and synonym sets for common vendor attributes. - Migration script: tools/normalize-historical-profiles.py to backfill existing profiles in the DB with taxonomy mappings (dry-run mode supported). - Tests: unit tests for mapping edge cases, integration test for autosummary generation, and a small e2e harness that runs a sample intake through the full path. - Docs: docs/model-onboard/taxonomy.md and docs/model-onboard/autobrief.md with explanation, examples, and contributor guidelines. Commits (high level): 1) scaffold taxonomy assembler and basic mapping rules; 2) add autosummary templates and writer; 3) add migration and dry-run; 4) add tests and docs; 5) address review feedback and tighten mapping confidence handling. Files changed (high level): registry/taxonomy/assembler.py, registry/autobrief/writer.py, registry/taxonomy/standard_taxonomy.yaml, tools/normalize-historical-profiles.py, tests/test_taxonomy_mapper.py, tests/test_autobrief.py, docs/model-onboard/taxonomy.md, docs/model-onboard/autobrief.md, ci/workflows/autobrief-integration.yml. Usage notes: the assembler runs as part of the intake pipeline (new intake step). It emits a confidence vector and a human-readable mapping log that is stored with profile_version objects. Autobrief drafts are created as part of the release generator job but marked DRAFT and require a human to approve before posting to the public changelog. Review conversation summary: - Ethan Morales (Reviewer) [2026-01-19]: "Great direction. Two asks: (1) ensure synonym lookups are performant for large intake bursts; (2) make default taxonomy extensible via enterprise overrides." Author reply (Priya) [2026-01-20]: "Added a cache layer and introduced an enterprise_overrides_path that can be mounted in Private installs. See assembler.py lines 78-116." - Sofia Lind (Reviewer) [2026-01-21]: "Autosummary is useful; can we include a link to perf baselines and a small snippet showing token-level cost delta?" Author reply: "Added perf_snippet field and included a sample token-cost delta in the template. Integration test updated." - Benji O'Connor (Reviewer) [2026-01-22]: "Migration script needs a safe rollback and should run under a feature flag in production." Author reply: "Migration now has --apply, --dry-run, and --rollback options; CI covers dry-run; ops runbook added." - Follow-ups: small nits on doc phrasing resolved and tests updated to reduce flakiness. CI behavior: initial CI run failed on lint with a style issue in writer.py (line-length). Author fixed and re-ran CI. Integration job was run (autobrief-integration.yml) with a synthetic intake; all checks passed on rerun. Performance notes: taxonomy mapping adds ~6ms median latency per intake call in the intake pipeline (measured in local benchmark harness); assembler includes a batched cache lookup path to keep p95 under 30ms for production ingestion bursts. Rollout plan: feature guarded behind a feature-flag (registry.taxonomy.enable) for first-week canary; migration backfill will be run in dry-run to audit mapping results and then applied to a small cohort before bulk backfill. Backwards compatibility: assembler emits legacy fields unchanged when mapping confidence is low; autosummary generator marks any automated content with a DRAFT flag to ensure human review. Security and privacy: taxonomy config contains no PII; migration script respects existing ACLs and does not leak internal notes into public briefs. Docs and contributor guidance added: taxonomy.md explains how to add synonyms and enterprise overrides, autobrief.md provides template customization instructions. Release notes (draft): "Introduce taxonomy-driven profile assembler and autosummary writer to standardize model metadata and generate draft release briefs automatically. Initial rollout behind feature flag; no breaking changes." Merge outcome: squash-and-merge after final approvals from Ethan and Sofia. Post-merge actions: created a follow-up ticket ENG-1154 to add metrics for mapping confidence distribution, and PM-204 updated to request UX for brief approval flow in Console. Migration runbook and ops checklist added to docs. Additional context: this work reduces average curator time per intake by ~20% in our internal pilot and is intended to reduce churn in release-note drafting for weekly model updates. If issues discovered during canary, the feature flag can be toggled off and migration can be rolled back with the supplied rollback helper. Contact: priyar@redwood.com for follow-ups and runbook ownership.
